rationale: vcirc is a very small C++ program (13 functions, 209 total text bytes) built from tiny virtual-dispatch-heavy methods (Point/Circle show, hide, move, expand), so the priority is cheap, per-function transformations that add signal without bloating the minuscule text section: SUB gets the highest weights because the arithmetic in MoveTo/Expand coordinates is ideal for instruction substitution with near-zero risk, and IBR is similarly favored since replacing plain branches with indirect ones defeats naive disassembly at negligible cost on such small control-flow graphs; SPLIT earns moderate weight because splitting the few multi-block functions increases structural diversity essentially for free, while ICALL is given moderate weight to convert direct virtual/auxiliary calls into indirect ones for call-graph obfuscation, tempered by its nonzero risk on small dispatch-heavy code; BCF and FLA are discouraged (high SizeCost/RuntimeCost weights) because bogus-control-flow flattening inflates a 209-byte text region disproportionately and flattening is both overhead-heavy and low-yield on 8-70 byte function bodies; IGV is effectively disabled (near-zero gains, high risk/cost) since the program has no large control-flow graph to desynchronize and its global-variable tricks would only add fragility to a trivial program; correctness risk is kept low across the favored passes because virtual-dispatch-heavy OO code is sensitive to call- and control-flow-level transformations.
